content.title: Jamie Dixon questions technical foul after Duke win over TCU: ‘I didn’t say anything bad’
content.text: SportsPublished: Mar. 21, 2026, 9:25 p.m.TCU coach Jamie Dixon on the sideline during Saturday's game against TCU. (Photo by Jared C. Tilton/Getty Images)Getty ImagesBy Matt Connolly | mconnolly@pennlive.comDuke pulled away for an 81-58 win over TCU Saturday in the second round of the NCAA Tournament, thanks in part to a technical foul call on Horned Frogs coach Jamie Dixon that came at an inopportune time.The Blue Devils were leading 59-50 with under 10 minutes remaining when Duke forward Maliq Brown appeared to commit a goaltending violation on a shot attempt by TCU’s Tanner Toolson.Minutes later, Dixon was called for a technical foul by official Paul Szelc as he questioned the call. Dixon was asked about the technical and what led to it after the game.“I didn’t get set off; I had a conversation with him,” the former Pitt coach said. “There was no raising of voice. It was a conversation, as he asked for. You know, what are you going to do? “I mean obviously we know what it was. Everybody knows what it was. Just, you know, what can you say? What can you say?”If goaltending had been called, TCU would have cut Duke’s lead to 59-52. Instead, the Blue Devils continued to pull away, adding two points on the technical free throws.Duke ended up going on a 13-0 run to put the game away.“It’s a big play, big play. And then you compound it. I didn’t cuss. I didn’t say anything bad. I had a conversation with him. It had a huge impact on the game,” Jamie Dixon said.Duke, the No. 1 overall seed in the NCAA Tournament, now advances to the Sweet 16.
